what_works: High-performing videos consistently center on Indian pride, national security, geopolitical rivalry, and strategic wealth: 'India's Highest-Earning Cities' (3,516 views), 'दुनिया के Top 5 सबसे Powerful देश' (3,436 views), 'Mystery of the 1962 War' (2,618 views), 'India’s Maritime Boundary' (2,315 views).
Listicles, direct face-offs, and comparisons dramatically outpull obscure solo historical anecdotes (e.g., Top 5 powerful nations, India vs China, US vs North Korea).

Custom thumbnails correlate strongly with reach: top 7 videos except one utilized custom thumbnails, while almost all bottom 10 videos had none (sample size is small, but the correlation is distinct).
High performers feature curiosity-inducing, provocative Hinglish titles with emotional triggers (😲, 😱, 🔥, 'चौंका देंगी', 'असली बादशाह').

diagnosis.hook: Weak videos rely on academic questions ('Photosynthesis Explained', 'How a Mud Wall Stopped an Empire') or answer the mystery in the title itself. Script hooks in weak shorts ask rhetorical textbook questions ('Can just 78 people alone shake the power...') rather than triggering visual shock or cognitive dissonance.
diagnosis.buildup: Underperforming scripts resemble Wikipedia recaps cluttered with complex dates, places, and ruler names (e.g., 'In 1019 AD', 'Dharmapala of Dandabhukti', 'Fazl Khan') rather than escalating tension beat-by-beat toward a payoff.
diagnosis.visuals: Metadata confirms weak videos omit custom thumbnails (`has_custom_thumbnail: false`). For animated or asset-driven shorts, heavy reliance on mismatched uniforms ('indian', 'mongol') and static battle recaps without dynamic map overlays or kinetic visual changes kills pacing.
diagnosis.titles_topics: Severe topical mismatch. TruFact's audience responds to Indian geopolitics, defense, rankings, and surprising India-centric facts. Shifting abruptly to world history battles (Myeongnyang, Roman concrete, Sacred Cats) or basic biology (Photosynthesis, Mantis Shrimp) alienates the channel's algorithm authority.
diagnosis.other: Language inconsistency: The top performers are framed in Hindi/Hinglish with cultural context, while the lowest performers are titled in sterile standard English.

hook_rules: Open in the first 2 seconds with an unbelievable visual claim or contradiction, never with dates, names, or generic rhetorical questions like 'Do you know?'.
Create an open curiosity gap: reveal the stakes immediately, but aggressively withhold the specific resolution until the final 5 seconds.
Use high-arousal audio-visual hooks: pair the first line with a sound effect (thud, siren, clash) and on-screen bold keyword captions in contrasting yellow/red.
Frame Indian history around David vs. Goliath stakes (e.g., 'How 300 soldiers humiliated an entire European armada') instead of naming dates.
Never give the answer in the title or the opening sentence (e.g., avoid 'Concrete heals itself' or '78 people').
buildup_rules: Cut down proper nouns: replace obscure names and dates with roles (e.g., replace 'General Araiyan at Sakkarakkottam' with 'The Emperor's fiercest general').
Adopt a three-act escalation framework: Act 1 (The Impossible Odds), Act 2 (The Disastrous Twist/Counter-Attack), Act 3 (The Shocking Climax).
Ensure every beat changes the state of the story: every 5-7 seconds must present an escalation, obstacle, or plot turn.
End on a definitive punchline or philosophical kicker rather than trailing off into encyclopedia dates and administrative summaries.
visual_rules: Always set a high-contrast custom thumbnail featuring an expressive face, saturated red/yellow arrows, or high-stakes iconography.
Change on-screen visual assets, zoom level, or angle at minimum every 2.0 to 2.5 seconds to prevent visual drop-off.
Use kinetic map animations, dynamic boundary highlights, and zoom-ins rather than static portraits of rulers or plain text screens.
Ensure text overlays are large, center-screen or upper-third, dual-color (e.g., white with yellow emphasis), and limited to 3-5 words per graphic.
title_rules: Adopt a Hinglish format combining clear Hindi keywords with punchy English words (e.g., 'भारत की वो जंग जिसने पूरी दुनिया को हिला दिया! 😱').
Keep titles under 55 characters so nothing gets truncated on mobile feeds.
Include exactly 1-2 emotionally evocative emojis (🇮🇳, 😱, 🚀, ⚔️) and high-CTR words like 'खुलासा', 'सच', 'Secret', 'Impossible'.
Avoid raw metadata leaks like 'Description:' or repetitive hashtags inside the title string.
topic_rules: Stick strictly to the core channel pillar: Indian Geopolitics, Military & Defense, High-Stakes Indian History, and Comparative Country Rankings.
Validate every topic against mass relatability: discard obscure foreign battles, generic classroom science, and over-told textbook syllabus topics.
Focus on untold or counter-intuitive angles of well-known themes (e.g., secret military operations, economic power plays, hidden border conflicts).
avoid: Generic school biology and science trivia (e.g., Photosynthesis, Mantis Shrimp, animal trivia).
Academic textbook phrasing in titles ('The Battle of...', 'Explained', 'True Story of...').
Overloading scripts with dates (e.g., 'In September 1660', 'On March 12, 1930') and hard-to-pronounce historical names.
Uploading videos without an enticing custom thumbnail frame.
Revealing the climax or solution in the title, thumbnail, or first 3 seconds.
